## Why this matters
The battles of Issus and Gaugamela decided who would rule the largest empire of its time [1].

## Issus, 333 BC
At Issus, Darius III chose a narrow coastal plain that cancelled out his larger army [1, 2].

## Gaugamela, 331 BC
Two years later Darius picked open ground, but Alexander's cavalry charge broke through the Persian centre [2].

## Recap
- Issus was fought on terrain that favoured the smaller Macedonian army.
- Gaugamela was Darius's last great attempt to stop Alexander.
- After Gaugamela, the Persian heartland lay open.
